artifact: ADVI_BDPARITY roster reconciliation -- qt6 215 vs export 201, ADJUDICATED

RESULT_THE_ROSTER_GAP_IS_IMMATERIAL.verdict: The 15 qt6-only groups total 8,557,079.70 = 0.08 pct of all-group Aug EMV. They are all person-named groups, largest 2,525,985.21, smallest 11,306.85 -- no house/ops bucket among them. THEREFORE the 215-vs-201 group-roster difference CANNOT explain the ~2.09B L1-L3 gap. The gap is WITHIN the 200 shared groups -- missing ACCOUNTS beneath groups the export already has, not missing groups. This SHARPENS the membership finding rather than competing with it.

HAZARD_PORTFOLIO_GROUP_MARKET_VALUE.observation: The export column named 'Portfolio Group Market Value' is NOT a group-level total. It is single-valued in only 22 of 201 groups; specimen group Boston Prachyl carries 109 DISTINCT values across 211 rows. Even on the 21-group clean subset where it IS single-valued, it ties qt6 EMV 0 of 21 times (spread -27.42 pct to +48.58 pct).
HAZARD_PORTFOLIO_GROUP_MARKET_VALUE.what_I_do_NOT_claim: I have NOT established what grain it is at. Reported as an observation, not a mechanism.
HAZARD_PORTFOLIO_GROUP_MARKET_VALUE.why_it_matters: A column whose NAME asserts a group total while its VALUES vary 109 ways inside one group is a name-vs-computation trap. Do not aggregate it with first()/max() as a group MV -- I did exactly that in a first pass and it produced a median +2,627 pct difference that was pure artifact of my own aggregation. That comparison is WITHDRAWN.

AUTHORING_NOTE_F010: This file was first written from a python -c string inside a double-quoted bash command.
